summary: Dedicated capacity throughput erosion from thin-provisioned background validation sweeps
description: Issue summary: BrightLens reported a gradual but sustained throughput degradation on their Dedicated pool starting 2026-03-09 11:00 UTC. Impact: p50 throughput down ~20%, p95 latency increased from 180ms to ~650ms, and periodic 5xx attach timeouts for short streams. Customer-facing APIs experienced elevated error rates and request queuing. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs), prod (us-west primarily), mixed batch/stream workload with many short-lived streams. Steps to reproduce: 1) Route a steady burst of short streams (100ms token streams) plus periodic background model-validate sweeps (internal sweep job). 2) Observe allocation attach times and autoscaler behavior via /metrics and pool allocator logs. 3) Note degradation begins when sweep concurrency > 4 and persists until sweep finish. Observed metrics & logs: - Autoscaler shows multiple rapid scale-ups followed by scale-downs (oscillation) with node attach latencies spiking. - GPU attach failures return transient 504/5xx. - KV cache hit-rate drops during sweep windows, warmups collide with incoming traffic. - Background job logs show model-validation workers launching concurrent inference processes on the same pool (sweep-runner-37@us-west-2). Hypothesis: Thin provisioning for background validation sweeps is contending for reserved GPU slots and the autoscaler interprets the sweep workload as customer demand, causing oscillatory scaling and transient GPU unavailability for tenant requests. Additionally, the sweep workload forces repeated KV cache evictions/warmups that increase per-inference latency. Impact scale: Customer production traffic degraded for ~3 hours across peak windows. Workarounds attempted by customer: throttling their internal sweep frequency reduced symptoms but did not eliminate intermittent attach errors. Links: - Grafana: dashboards/shared/brightlens-dedicated-pool - Logs: splunk:prod/allocator/2026-03-09/brightlens - Slack: #support (thread t:brightlens-dedicated-20260309)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC: Support triaged with customer, reproduced locally using a modeled workload that includes short streams + concurrent validation sweeps.
2026-03-10 11:02 UTC: Observed autoscaler state machine flip-flopping when sweep concurrency exceeded 3; rapid attach requests saturated attachment queue leading to attach timeouts.
Examined allocator logs: saw repeated 'attach request queued' and 'gpu-attach-timeout' entries correlated with sweep-runner pids.
KV cache telemetry: frequent misses and 'kv_cache_evict' spikes during sweeps; memory pressure led to longer model load times on GPUs.

Hypothesis refined: background validation processes create short high-density connection bursts that look like ephemeral tenant bursts; autoscaler reaction thresholds treat this as organic demand and provision GPUs, but the provisioned GPUs are immediately used by sweeps and not made available to tenant streams due to affinity/priority rules.
Cross-check: no infra-wide driver crashes or HBM faults; hardware health looks nominal. Not a CUDA driver regression.
Related historical ticket with similar autoscale oscillation observed: SUP-77109 (note: different root cause but similar autoscaler dynamics).
comments: Support (Asha Patel) 2026-03-10 09:30: Thanks for reporting — we've scoped this as a P1. We can reproduce with a simulation. Asking Eng to look at autoscaler thresholds and sweep job tagging.

Customer (BrightLens - Maya Chen) 2026-03-10 10:02: Their ops team confirmed they ran a nightly model-validate sweep at 10:45 PST which lines up with the onset. They're willing to coordinate a test where they reduce sweep concurrency.

SRE (Ethan Morales) 2026-03-10 11:45: Initial mitigation: throttle sweep concurrency to 1 for BrightLens namespace and enabled temporary allocation priority for tenant traffic. Early data shows p50 latency recovered ~12%. We need a permanent fix.

Eng (Ravi Kumar) 2026-03-11 08:20: Proposed changes: 1) Tag sweep-runner jobs with 'low-priority' so autoscaler can deprioritize them, 2) add a short debounce to autoscaler scale decisions for ephemeral short-stream bursts, 3) adjust KV cache warmup throttling to avoid large simultaneous warmups.
Support (Asha Patel) 2026-03-11 14:00: Customer confirmed reduced errors after throttling. Planning a coordinated weekend change window for autoscaler tweak + sweep tagging.
Customer (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12 09:05: Appreciative of progress. Asked if there's a best-practice doc for scheduling internal validation sweeps to avoid impacting production traffic.
resolution: Workaround: temporary mitigation applied 2026-03-10: BrightLens throttled their sweep concurrency and we applied a soft-priority tagging for their sweep-runner processes; result: throughput recovered to within 95% of baseline and attach timeouts dropped significantly. Permanent remediation plan: - Short term (scheduled): deploy autoscaler debounce to ignore spikey short-stream bursts under 10s for 48-hour pilot. - Medium term: implement job-priority tagging and scheduler changes so background validation workers are placed on separate capacity pools or throttled when tenant SLA traffic is present. - Long term: provide customers with a 'validation-sweep best practices' doc and an API to mark non-customer background jobs so they don't influence autoscaler. Follow-ups: schedule post-deploy monitoring window and revert plan if regressions appear. Related PRs: autoscaler PR #906 implements debounce and tagging support.
